diagnostic_evidence.quote: \begin{theorem}[Koopman invariance of Sobolev spaces]\label{thm:hs_frac_charac} Assume that the condition \eqref{e:L1} holds.
Its proof follows from the more general result of \Cref{thm:hs_frac_charac}.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated proof is by thm:hs_frac_charac, whose global hypothesis is condition (L^1), but thm:diff_density_hs_invariance does not assume that condition. The displayed L2 regularity of p does not imply the L-infinity marginal bound required by (L^1), so the cited theorem cannot be applied as written. The conclusion can instead be proved directly from the Hilbert–Schmidt estimates furnished by the L2 derivatives of p, but that argument is not supplied.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either add condition (L^1) to the theorem and its application, or supply the direct argument that the L2 bounds on the x-derivatives of p map L2 boundedly into H^ell and then interpolate.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised density-only sufficient condition and its truncated-normal application are unsupported by the stated dependency.
issues.title: Density-based invariance theorem invokes a result without its standing hypothesis
issues.why_classification: Preserving the density-only scope requires a contained but nontrivial replacement argument; merely adding (L^1) would weaken the stated sufficient condition.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Replacing $H^1$ by $H^\ell$ in the arguments from step 1 from \eqref{eq:h1_bound} onward, we get \eqref{e:hl_charac} for $\ell \in \bN$.

issues.failure_explanation: The characterization requires an H^{-|alpha|} estimate for each alpha, including an L2 estimate when alpha=0. The higher-order proof instead pairs only with H^ell and obtains H^{-ell}, while Step 1 even records H^{-1} for alpha=0. Since H^{-ell} is generally larger than H^{-|alpha|}, these estimates do not imply the stated condition. Conversely, deriving the necessary H^{-|alpha|} bounds requires first proving boundedness on the intermediate Sobolev spaces, not merely replacing H1 by Hell.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reorganize the proof to obtain boundedness on every intermediate H^r by interpolation before proving necessity, and use the displayed L2 estimate for the density case to obtain all required H^{-|alpha|} bounds.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed necessary-and-sufficient characterization, its fractional consequence, and results that invoke that characterization are not proved as written.
issues.title: Sobolev characterization proof establishes the wrong negative-order norms
issues.why_classification: The conclusion may be recoverable, but doing so requires a substantive reorganization of the interpolation and duality argument rather than a routine algebraic edit.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Recall the bounded domain $\Omega \subset \R^n$ with Lipschitz boundary

issues.failure_explanation: For a general n-dimensional Lipschitz domain, H^1 does not embed into C_b unless the Sobolev smoothness exceeds n/2. Likewise, arbitrary finite measures, such as point masses, do not all belong to H^{-1} in dimensions n>=2. The displayed chain is therefore false in the paper's stated general-dimensional setting.

failure_location.quote: we have the following chain of inclusions with continuous embeddings $H^1\,\subset\,C_b\,\subset\,L^2\,\subset\,C_b^* = \calM\,\subset\,H^{-1}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict this chain to dimensions and smoothness orders for which Sobolev embedding and measure inclusion hold, or replace it with the valid dimension-dependent embeddings.
issues.overall_effect: The paper gives an incorrect description of the function-space and dual-space embeddings outside the one-dimensional regime.
issues.title: Dimension-independent Sobolev embedding chain is false
issues.why_classification: The claim is locally correctable and the main estimates do not otherwise rely on the entire displayed chain.

The proof itself uses lambda as a strictly positive lower bound for the smallest eigenvalue, which is unavailable at lambda=0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require lambda>0 in cor:mc_error1_tikh and in every downstream result using the d/lambda bound; treat lambda=0 separately with thm:mc_error1.
issues.overall_effect: The regularized probabilistic and total-error guarantees are undefined at an expressly included parameter value.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For numerical stability, we apply a Tikhonov regularization with parameter $\lambda$ as in \eqref{eq:regularized_mcemdmd}

issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm requires lambda but always computes the unregularized inverse K_X^{-1}, so its output is independent of lambda and is not the regularized estimator used in the stated numerical methodology. The later displayed implementation is itself inconsistent, using (K_X^{-1}+lambda I)^{-1} on only one side rather than the defined (K_X+lambda I)^{-1}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use (K_X+lambda I)^{-1} on both sides in the algorithm and subsequent implementation formula, then recompute any experiments claimed to use that regularization.
issues.overall_effect: The executable construction does not implement the claimed regularized method, so the reported dependence on lambda and the numerical-stability procedure are not supported by the supplied algorithm.
issues.title: The advertised regularization parameter is not used by the kEDMD algorithm
issues.why_classification: The formula is locally repairable, but validating the numerical claims requires rerunning the computations with a materially different estimator.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In all cases, we consider the nonlinear observable $f(x) = e^x$.

issues.failure_explanation: For the chosen observable f(x)=e^x, the required ground truth is an average of f(y_l)=e^{y_l}. The algorithm instead averages y_l, estimating the Koopman action on the identity observable. Consequently, the subsequent error compares the kEDMD estimate for f with ground truth for a different observable.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace each summand y_l by f(y_l), consistently use m_truth as the summation limit, and rerun the numerical experiments and resulting comparisons.
issues.overall_effect: All empirical L-infinity errors, plots, and numerical comparisons produced by the stated procedure are invalid for the advertised observable.
issues.title: Numerical ground truth averages states instead of the observable
issues.why_classification: Although the algorithmic formula has a simple correction, every reported numerical result based on the erroneous ground truth must be recomputed.
